answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a signal as the anchor of the cost.
